links.outcome: Pathology VLM output stability under adversarial visual-semantic perturbations
links.effect: PathGLS Stability dimension measures output variance under adversarial perturbations; PathGLS sensitivity dropped 40.2% for hallucinated reports versus 2.1% for BERTScore.
links.quote: Specifically, on the Quilt-1M dataset, PathGLS reveals a steep sensitivity drop of 40.2% for hallucinated reports compared to only 2.1% for BERTScore.

unlisted_practices: Reference-free automated evaluation metric (grounding, logic, stability) for pathology VLM hallucination detection without ground truth

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an automated, reference-free monitoring/evaluation guardrail (PathGLS) designed to detect hallucinations and instability in pathology vision-language models prior to or during deployment.

primary.practice: reference-free multi-dimensional consistency evaluation and hallucination monitoring
